• Art 24(2) excludes only non-workers → Art 24(1) and Art 7(2) Reg 492/2011 apply.
• Never worked: Art 21(1) TFEU is conditional — after three months sufficient resources + sickness insurance (Art 7(1)(b)); without them no equal treatment (Art 24(1); Dano C-333/13).

cards.q: Case — Glass bottle cartel: Glasform AG (Austria), Vitra SA (France) and Bottelo BV (Netherlands, wholly state-owned), together 75% of the EU glass-bottle market, met at trade fairs in 2019–2024 and informally agreed common price increases and which customers in which Member State each would serve; nothing was signed. Glasform argues that Bottelo, as a state-owned company, is not an undertaking, that the arrangement was not legally binding, and that bottle prices actually fell during the period. (a) Did the companies infringe Article 101(1) TFEU? (3 points)
cards.a:
Yes: the three undertakings formed a by-object price-fixing and customer-sharing cartel (Art 101(1) TFEU).
• Undertaking: any entity engaged in an economic activity, regardless of legal status and financing (Höfner C-41/90); Art 106(1) → state-owned Bottelo covered.
• Agreement: concurrence of wills; form and binding force irrelevant → gentlemen's agreement suffices (ACF Chemiefarma 41/69), at least concerted practice.
• Object: Art 101(1)(a) prices, (c) customer sharing; appreciable without concrete effects (Expedia C-226/11) → falling prices irrelevant.
• Trade between Member States affected: cross-border cartel, 75% EU share.

cards.q: Case — Glass bottle cartel: Glasform AG (Austria), Vitra SA (France) and Bottelo BV (Netherlands, wholly state-owned), together 75% of the EU glass-bottle market, met at trade fairs in 2019–2024 and informally agreed common price increases and which customers in which Member State each would serve; nothing was signed. On 10 March 2026 the Commission, by a decision addressed to the three, found an infringement of Art 101 TFEU and fined Glasform €120 million. The decision was notified to Glasform on Thursday 12 March 2026. Glasform claims it was never given the opportunity to reply to the Commission's objections. (c) Is an action for annulment admissible (court, standing, time limit), and on which grounds? (3 points)
cards.a:
Yes: admissible at the General Court until 22 May 2026; ground: essential procedural requirement.
• Binding Commission decision (Art 288(4)), reviewable (Art 263(1) TFEU); General Court (Art 256(1)).
• Standing: addressee, Art 263(4) first alternative → no Plaumann; legal interest (fine).
• Two months from notification (Art 263(6)) = 12 May, +10 days distance (Art 60 RP GC).
• Grounds (Art 263(2)): incompetence, essential procedural requirement, Treaty/rule-of-law infringement, misuse of powers.
• Right to be heard (Art 27(1) Reg 1/2003, Art 41(2)(a) Charter) breached → void (Art 264(1)).

cards.q: Case — Glass bottle cartel: Glasform AG (Austria), Vitra SA (France) and Bottelo BV (Netherlands, wholly state-owned), together 75% of the EU glass-bottle market, met at trade fairs in 2019–2024 and informally agreed common price increases and which customers in which Member State each would serve; nothing was signed. On 10 March 2026 the Commission, by a decision addressed to the three, found an infringement of Art 101 TFEU and fined Glasform €120 million. Glasform's total worldwide turnover in 2025 was €1 billion. Glasform asks the General Court to reduce the fine and wants to know whether it must pay before judgment. (d) On what legal basis was the fine imposed, is its amount lawful, and what can the General Court do? (2 points)
cards.a:
€120m exceeds the 10% cap; the General Court can reduce it.
• Basis: Art 103(2)(a) TFEU → Art 23(2)(a) Reg 1/2003 (intent/negligence).
• Cap: 10% of preceding business year's total turnover = €100m → breach of rule of law.
• Art 261 TFEU, Art 31 Reg 1/2003: unlimited jurisdiction — cancel, reduce, increase.
• Art 278: no suspensory effect → pay or guarantee unless suspended.

cards.q: Case — Glass bottle cartel: Glasform AG (Austria), Vitra SA (France) and Bottelo BV (Netherlands, wholly state-owned), together 75% of the EU glass-bottle market, met at trade fairs in 2019–2024 and informally agreed common price increases and which customers in which Member State each would serve; nothing was signed. On 10 March 2026 the Commission, by a decision addressed to the three, found an infringement of Art 101 TFEU and fined Glasform €120 million. Brauhaus Wien AG, a brewery that bought bottles from Glasform at cartel prices, sues Glasform before the Vienna Commercial Court for the overcharge. Glasform's annulment action is still pending. (e) Can Brauhaus obtain damages, and how must the Vienna court treat the Commission decision? (2 points)
cards.a:
Yes: anyone harmed by a cartel can claim full compensation (Courage C-453/99, Manfredi C-295/04).
• Art 101: horizontal direct effect (BRT v SABAM 127/73).
• Directive 2014/104: actual loss, lost profit, interest (Art 3(2)); cartel harm presumed (Art 17(2)); joint-and-several liability (Art 11(1)).
• Art 16(1) Reg 1/2003: no ruling counter to the decision; pending annulment → stay or refer (Art 267, Masterfoods C-344/98).
